Workers with Mexico's Social Security Institute are set to march in Nuevo Laredo this afternoon as part of a national day of protest, with the local march scheduled to start at 3:30 p.m. at Plaza Hidalgo — known as Plaza del Reloj — and end at Plaza Esteban Baca Calderón, according to Claro Sports.

The Nuevo Laredo action is one of at least 16 states joining the October 30 mobilization by active and retired IMSS workers, who are pressing for a 10 percent raise applied directly to their base salary, better working conditions, and a reliable supply of medicines and medical supplies, according to the report. Protesters are also calling for the removal of Rafael Olivos Hernández, secretary general of the National Union of Social Security Workers (SNTSS).

The dispute centers on the size and shape of the raise. IMSS Director General Zoé Robledo has proposed an overall 8 percent increase, made up of 4 percent to base salary and 4 percent for housing assistance, according to Claro Sports. The dissident workers argue that split does not meet their demand for the full 10 percent on base pay.

In Mexico City, the national mobilization includes a morning march from IMSS headquarters on Paseo de la Reforma and an afternoon gathering at the National Medical Center Siglo XXI. A national assembly is planned for Saturday, October 31, according to the report.

For Nuevo Laredo residents, the practical takeaway is timing and place: the local march is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. from Plaza Hidalgo to Plaza Esteban Baca Calderón. A related gathering is also planned in Reynosa, on Boulevard Hidalgo, though no time was specified in the report.

Update — October 31, 2026

The national assembly planned for October 31 has now produced its next step. Dissident IMSS workers held their constitutive national assembly in Mexico City on October 31, with delegational representation from 17 states, and announced a fourth national megamarch for Monday, November 9, at 3:00 p.m., from the National Medical Center Siglo XXI to the Zócalo in Mexico City, according to El Sol de México and other reports of the assembly. A second national assembly is scheduled for Sunday, November 8, at 10:00 a.m. at Section 9 of the CNTE in Mexico City. The assembly ratified a seven-point petition, including a 10 percent raise applied directly to base pay, sufficient supplies, equipment and staffing, a universal retirement and pension regime, rejection of the Afore retirement-fund system, a health budget of at least 7 percent of GDP, elimination of the so-called gag law, and the removal of SNTSS secretary general Rafael Olivos Hernández and the calling of an extraordinary national congress. No agreement with authorities was reported; the workers said they had not reached agreements on their demands. The assembly announcements covered the national march; no Nuevo Laredo-specific action was reported.

Update — November 9, 2026

The fourth national megamarch called for today is underway. IMSS workers set out at 3:00 p.m. from the National Medical Center Siglo XXI toward the Zócalo in Mexico City, with a stop planned in front of the Senate, according to live reporting. Mexico City’s mobilization agenda estimated about 3,000 participants. No response from authorities or outcome had been reported as of this update; no Nuevo Laredo-specific action was reported.
